newsitem.title: USA: Bill Cosby returns to work on TV show.
newsitem.headline: Bill Cosby returns to work on TV show.

text.p: Entertainer Bill Cosby on Monday returned to work on his TV show for the first time since his son was murdered on a Los Angeles freeway earlier this month.
"He won't be coming out and making any statements," CBS spokeswoman Liz Josephson told reporters and TV news crews gathered outside the Kaufman-Astoria Studios in the New York City borough of Queens.
Cosby, a comedian, actor and author, arrived at the studio early on Monday morning to work on the situation comedy "Cosby" which airs on CBS. Monday's taping of the show was closed to spectators.

Ennis Cosby, 27, was shot in the head as he changed a tire on a Los Angeles freeway early on the morning of Jan. 16. A woman who saw part of the attack gave police a description of the killer as a white male wearing a knit cap, and that was used to put together a composite drawing of the suspect.
In an interview broadcast on CBS News on Sunday, Cosby said that his wife Camille was concerned that the killer was still free.
"There's a difference in this house," Cosby said in the interview. "Mrs. Cosby wants this man. I mean she verbalizes she wants him. She wants him now."
"She refuses to accept the fact that this 'thing' is still out there," Cosby continued. "She doesn't accept the fact that nobody comes forward to help with the truth."
But the grieving Cosby said it was also time to get back to work and find humour again.

"I think it's time for me to tell the people that we have to laugh. We've got to laugh. But I just want the people to know -- those who watch me, those who are with me -- it's over for looking at me to do anything but go back to that which I am," he said.
In further excerpts of the interview broadcast by the network on Monday, an emotional Cosby described burying his son in an herb garden at the family home in Massachusetts.
"We set the coffin down over the hole and I said, 'We now want to give praise to God for allowing us to know him, not for giving him to us but just letting us know him,'" Cosby said.
Cosby said he had complete confidence in the Los Angeles police investigators but in light of the O.J. Simpson trial, he spoke about the judicial process.
"When they find him, I want it laid out, I don't want just the blood dropped in the sock and everything," Cosby said in an allusion to the O.J. Simpson investigation.

In another excerpt of the interview broadcast later by CBS News Radio and on the CBS "This Morning" television programme, Cosby denied being the father of a woman who, along with a male friend, have been charged with trying to extort $40 million from the entertainer.
Cosby acknowledged however, that he had had a rendezvous with the woman's mother. He said the birth certificate of the woman claiming to be his daughter listed someone else as her father.

The woman, Autumn Jackson, 22, and Jose Medina, 51, were arrested nine days ago on charges they demanded money from Cosby to keep them from selling a story to a tabloid newspaper alleging that Jackson was the entertainer's illegitimate daughter.

According to court papers, Jackson was one of many young people for whom Cosby paid educational expenses for several years. Federal prosecutors have said there was no evidence the alleged scheme was connected with the murder of Cosby's son.
